beats.trigger: From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The hard part is not access; it is absorption.
beats.got: Buying the tool is the easy part. Getting people to use it is the hard part.

beats.trigger: Walk in with one example where people had access to a tool or process but real use did not follow.
beats.got: I have an example already: the ERP reporting module nobody opened.

beats.trigger: **Interview** for your teammate's job-to-be-done using the agentic Jobs-to-be-Done pattern
beats.got: nothing new. It is a list of verbs, and none of it has a cost or a payback attached.

beats.trigger: what makes you hesitate about actually handing this to them?
beats.got: A question about my feelings. I would answer it in one word and move on.

beats.trigger: Your teammate doesn't want your agent. They want a job done.
beats.got: Start from what the person needs, not from the tool. I can accept that.

beats.trigger: does it name one teammate, their current way of doing the job, and an outcome you could observe?
beats.got: A check I can use: one named person and an outcome I can observe. That is close to measurable.

beats.trigger: If the reason is merely *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: Don't justify a choice by the sunk cost of the licence. I agree with that.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it
beats.got: Find the one obstacle that matters, not all of them.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: One root cause instead of ten risks. That is useful for a board paper.

beats.trigger: Missing names remain visible as `UNASSIGNED — Monday's question`
beats.got: The plan shows where nobody owns anything. That is what I look for in a programme review. I rarely see it written down.

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plan is a hypothesis that needs testing. Fair.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: A good question for any investment case: what must be true for people to drop what they use today.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: A pre-mortem that ends in one named conversation and one test. That is concrete.

beats.trigger: Test the switch, not the solution.
beats.got: nothing new. It is a recap.

beats.trigger: The rest of this is about the person on the other end of your plan.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A candidate that does not move it is not a candidate.
beats.got: If it doesn't move the outcome, drop it. Sensible, though there is still no number.

beats.trigger: Hand someone the agent file and they run it, get a generic answer, and quietly stop.
beats.got: Buying a copy of the thing does not give you the know-how behind it. This is why the licence does not produce the benefit.

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all, which is why the product being sold as a shared agent is always three of the four parts
beats.got: A vendor sells three of four parts. The fourth, accountability, stays with whoever owns it. That is a risk named before I raised it.

beats.trigger: Many companies have rolled out access far ahead of trust.
beats.got: Seats deployed and people actually using it are two different numbers, and they usually get reported as one. That is exactly how my three digital programmes went wrong.

beats.trigger: Michael Polanyi, a philosopher of science, had the line for it: *we know more than we can tell.*
beats.got: People pick up what resembles what they already do. A philosopher was not needed for that.

beats.trigger: The interface is the first piece whose shape depends on somebody whose calendar you do not control.
beats.got: nothing new. It is abstract and I don't know what this piece refers to.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: A good analysis got no decision, because leadership hadn't done the work themselves and the priorities had moved on. I have sat in that meeting.

beats.trigger: Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
beats.got: The alternative is the current spreadsheet, not nothing. Any business case has to beat that baseline.

beats.trigger: Whether they pick it up is their decision, made for their own reasons, on a Tuesday you will not be in the room for.
beats.got: You can't force adoption.

beats.trigger: A missing name is a finding
beats.got: If nobody is named as owner, the thing is not real yet. I can use that as a test on any proposal.

beats.trigger: The agent reviews, rewrites the sharing artifact in place, and reports what changed.
beats.got: The agent tidies the file. This is process for the person running the exercise.

beats.trigger: Push back where the agent's summary is wrong.
beats.got: Don't accept the agent's summary without checking it. I would do that anyway.

beats.trigger: Access is easy; absorption is scarce.
beats.got: Four points. This is the one I keep.

beats.trigger: Come to Module 8 without one tested assumption or named person and you'll be reconstructing the contact
beats.got: Homework: one named person and one tested assumption.

beats.trigger: The sharing plan leaves the room and meets the organisation.
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Seats deployed and people actually using the tool are two different numbers. I'll ask for both whenever a tool is pitched.
Test any proposal with: who is the named owner, and what would have to be true for people to drop what they use today? A missing name means it's not real yet.
A vendor's 'shared agent' is three of four parts. Someone in the company still has to answer for it.

monday.move: Ask my controller who actually uses the month-end variance report and what they do instead of it. Then put the owner's name and one usage number on whatever AI tool IT proposes for finance.
monday.stop_condition: If nobody can be named as owner, or nobody can say what they do today, I don't take it further.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: I came in thinking AI is a licence you buy. The point that an agent file handed over gives a generic answer, and that access gets reported as if it were use, made me see why licences don't deliver. I'm not yet convinced that the organisation builds it. That would need a cost or payback figure, and I didn't get one.

one_line: Better than I expected, because it says rolling out a licence is not the same as people using it. But I still have no cost per month and no payback figure.
